name: Rofanplateau
kurzbeschreibung: The Rofanplateau is a unique high plateau with alpine meadows, mountain lakes, and breathtaking views over Achensee and the Alps.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Rofanplateau unfolds as a sun-drenched, dramatic high-alpine amphitheater in the Rofan Mountains, perched immediately east of Lake Achensee between 1,800 and 2,300 meters altitude. Standing in sharp geological contrast to the rolling valley floor, vertical limestone faces, knife-edge ridges, and towering summits like the Hochiss (2,299 m, highest peak of the Rofan), the Rofanspitze (2,259 m), the Seekarlspitze, and the Haidachstellwand dominate the skyline. Due to its sheer drop-offs, the plateau is famous for its "swallow's nest perspective": gaze straight down into the turquoise depths of Lake Achensee and across the Inn Valley to the glaciated spines of the Zillertal Alps. At the center of the plateau sits the historic Erfurter Hütte (1,831 m), nestled beside the top terminal of the Rofan Cable Car.

Route & Requirements

The high plateau caters seamlessly to casual day walkers and seasoned vertical climbers. A family-friendly favorite is the short hike from Erfurter Hütte up to the Gschöllkopf summit (2,039 m): a scenic gravel trail ascends in roughly 45 minutes to the "Adlerhorst" (Eagle's Nest) viewing platform, crafted from forged steel to resemble a giant eyrie suspended over limestone precipices (easy grade T1/T2). Mountain trekkers tackle the ascent of Mount Hochiss (2.5 hours round trip, 470 vertical meters, grade T2/T3) or traverse past pristine Lake Grubersee to the Rofanspitze. For vertical scramblers, the famous "Achensee 5-Peak Via Ferrata" links five distinct ferrata routes across Haidachstellwand, Rosskopf, Seekarlspitze, Spieljoch, and Hochiss (grades B to C/D), offering flexible day routes or an epic multi-peak traverse. Sturdy hiking boots, wind protection, and sun lotion are mandatory in this treeless alpine environment. Ferrata routes strictly require a helmet, harness, and certified lanyard set. Leashed dogs are welcome along hiking paths and aboard the cable car.

Visit & Arrival

By rail, travelers arrive via ÖBB mainline trains into Jenbach station, boarding frequent regional VVT bus line 4080 to the Maurach Rofanseilbahn stop. Motorists take the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wiesing/Achensee) and follow the B181 highway 5 kilometers north into Maurach. Free parking is available for cable car ticket holders at the lower terminal. The cable car runs daily between 8:30 AM and 5:00 PM.

Tips

Thrill-seekers should experience the "Airrofan Skyglider": suspended inside an eagle-shaped harness, riders plunge 200 vertical meters from the Gschöllkopf at speeds up to 80 km/h along an overhead wire. Afterwards, relax on the sun deck of Erfurter Hütte or rustic Mauritzalm for fluffy Tyrolean Kaiserschmarrn with panoramic lake views.
